html:
Alexios I Komnenos was Byzantine emperor from 1081 to 1118. He took over a collapsing empire and began its recovery, the Komnenian restoration. A young general from a military family, he seized Constantinople in a coup in 1081.

The empire was under attack on every side. The Seljuk Turks had overrun most of Anatolia after Manzikert in 1071, and the Normans under Robert Guiscard invaded the Balkans and beat him at Dyrrhachium in 1081. To get the help of the Venetian fleet he gave Venice the trade privileges of the Golden Bull. With Cuman allies he destroyed the Pechenegs at Levounion in 1091, and he restored the coinage with the gold hyperpyron.

His appeal to Pope Urban II for soldiers against the Turks helped set off the First Crusade in 1096. He used the crusaders to win back western Anatolia, but quarrelled with them over Antioch. His daughter Anna Komnene told his story in the Alexiad.
